correctness.rationale: Binary layer-cake reduces the Gini operator norm to nontrivial cut indicators. All dimension-three 254 nontrivial cuts fall into 13 automorphism/complement orbits with explicitly listed polynomial/piecewise ratios; the singleton gives gamma3=rho(15−rho²)/14 and gamma1=gamma2=rho. Lifting cylinder functions multiplies both Gini norms by four and gives gamma_d>=gamma3 for d>=3; Walsh characters give mean-zero L2 norm rho. Product convolution is Gini-nonexpansive and TV Dobrushin bounds gamma_d<=min(1,2(1−2^{-d})delta_d). Hellinger affinity of a column bounds lower ratio by 1−exp(−d rho²/8); its chi² divergence plus TV upper bound proves dichotomy d rho²→0/infinity. For rho sqrt(d)→a, log-likelihood CLT plus bounded second moments gives the *single-vertex* lognormal Gini profile 2Phi(a/sqrt2)−1; antipodal row CLT yields a separate upper bound for full gamma. Independent exhaustive all binary cut computations in d=1..4 for rho=.15,.55,.87 agreed for dimensions <=3; d4 tests are corroboration, not claimed exact all-rho norm.

The cutoff and distinguished Gaussian witness quantify a global nonlinear norm of a canonical independent-bit Markov kernel that is not identical to classical TV mixing or quadratic noise stability.
